text:
Cheng: quick heads-up — ran a small FP8/INT8 KV-only quant experiment on redwood-open-7b. Memory down ~28% on a4g but cold-start 95th latency jumped ~2.1x. paste of repro below.

Mia: rough numbers? is this on dedicated or hosted?

Cheng: dedicated pool (small dev cluster). baseline warm 95p ~210ms, fp8-kv 95p cold ~460ms. warm latencies look fine (~5-10% degradation).

Sam: did you quantize attention weights or just the KV cache?

Cheng: KV cache only. weights still fp16. config snippet: 
```
model: redwood-open-7b
quant: 
  kv_only: true
  backend: awq
  dtype: fp8
runtime:
  batch_size: 1
  kv_warmup: 32
  prefill_strategy: none
```

Ana: interesting — FP8 for kv can change memory layout and prefetch patterns. we saw similar tail jumps when prefill gets slow. did you use streaming responses?

Cheng: yes streaming on. pattern is lots of small requests -> cold keys on first few tokens -> high dequant cost. logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T15:22:01Z] INF kv_miss=1 dequant_ms=18 alloc_mb=4224 cold_lat_ms=478
[2026-03-18T15:22:01Z] INF kv_miss=0 dequant_ms=3 alloc_mb=3000 warm_lat_ms=220
```

Ryan: dequant_ms of 18ms per miss is big. is that scalar dequant per key or vectorized? backend?

Cheng: AWQ backend does per-chunk dequant; looks like we trigger fallback path for first access which isn't vectorized.

Mia: could we prefill or pre-dequant the first N keys during allocation? maybe run a background job to touch KVs for new instances.

Sam: we have kv_prefill flag but it increases startup memory and CPU. tradeoff. Have you tried kv_warmup 8/16/32 sweep?

Cheng: only 32 so far. I'll run 8/16 next. Also will try INT8-KV to compare dequant cost.

Ana: please also profile kernel calls. if AWQ dequant kernel isn't fused for our hw, switching to int8-kv (gptq path) might reduce per-key cost even if memory wins less.

InfraBot: new perf job scheduled: perf/job/1819004321-kv-flexquant-sweep (kv_warmup=[8,16,32], dtype=[fp8,int8], backend=[awq,gptq]) - ETA 2h

Ryan: add a test route that simulates PLG traffic: lots of 1-token completions with unique prefixes. that's where cold kv matters.

Cheng: good call. i'll push test harness and share results here. for triage checklist:
- reproduce on dedicated and hosted mirror
- sweep kv_warmup 8/16/32
- compare fp8-kv vs int8-kv (awq vs gptq)
- measure dequant_ms distribution and kernel type (scalar/vector)
- try prefill=background-touch and measure memory delta

Mia: ping me when results are in — I want to add a note to the model onboarding eval doc about KV-only quant caveats. :memo:

Sam: if int8-kv gives similar memory savings with <10% 95p tail, that might be default for PLG tier.

Cheng: ack. will update. first run (8 vs 16) queued. i'll drop numbers in ~2h.

Ana: also capture telemetry: cpu steal, memcpy stalls, and kernel: that helped us catch an mmap alignment issue last month.

Cheng: copying that checklist into the job metadata. thanks.

Ryan: note — if we go with prefill, add option to prefill asynchronously after route acceptance so token latency for the first response doesn't block.

Cheng: good idea. adding to follow-ups.

InfraBot: perf/job/1819004321-kv-flexquant-sweep started (run-id 20260318-001).

Mia: thanks — will monitor.

Cheng: updating thread when we have numbers. short term hypothesis: FP8-KV saves memory but AWQ dequant fallback on cold key access causes scalar dequant costs that spike cold tail.

Sam: thanks — bookmarking for design meeting next week. :thumbsup:
